# Switch supported time ranges and refresh portfolio performance context

> Prove that selecting any supported time-range value keeps exactly one active choice and refreshes the chart range, x-axis labels, and period comparison.

## Step 1

Open {{portfolio_overview_url}} in a browser and wait for the Portfolio Overview workspace to finish loading with the Portfolio Performance card visible.

## Step 2

Assert the workspace header's time-range segmented control shows 1D, 1W, 1M, 3M, YTD, 1Y, and ALL, with 1M as the only active value on first load.

## Step 3

capture baseline: current performance chart data range, visible x-axis labels, and displayed period comparison for the currently active time range.

## Step 4

For each time-range option 1D, 1W, 1M, 3M, YTD, 1Y, and ALL, select that option in the segmented control and confirm it becomes the only active value while the performance chart data range, visible x-axis labels, and displayed period comparison change from the captured baseline.

## Step 5 — assert @verifies ac-11, ac-12, ac-13, ac-15, ac-17

Confirm state-transition check: performance chart data range (changed-by) — the stated promise: Selecting a different time-range value updates the performance chart data range.

content.test_md_blob:
# Hover a performance point to inspect the custom tooltip

> Prove hovering a chart point shows the custom tooltip near the active point, updates the displayed date, portfolio value, benchmark value, and return, and leaves summary cards unchanged.

## Step 1

Open {{portfolio_overview_url}} in a browser and wait for the Portfolio Overview workspace to finish loading with the Portfolio Performance card visible.

## Step 2

On the Portfolio Overview page, store the current values shown in the dashboard summary cards as baseline_summary_cards and confirm no performance-chart tooltip is currently visible.

## Step 3

Store the pre-hover chart detail state as baseline_hover_state, including the absence of tooltip date, portfolio value, benchmark value, and return.

## Step 4

Hover a visible data point on the Portfolio Performance chart and inspect the hover state near the active point.

## Step 5

Assert a custom tooltip appears near the active point, the active point shows an outer ring and inner dot, the tooltip displays a date, portfolio value, benchmark value, and return that differ from baseline_hover_state, and the dashboard summary cards still match baseline_summary_cards.

## Step 6

Confirm the hover treatment is custom chart UI rather than a default browser or graph-library tooltip.

## Step 7 — assert @verifies ac-14, ac-24, ac-32, ac-33, ac-34, ac-35, ac-36, ac-37, ac-38, ac-40

Confirm propagation check: custom tooltip when hovering a chart point (exists) — the stated promise: Hovering a chart point shows the custom tooltip.

# Lock and unlock a selected performance point by clicking it

> Prove a chart point click locks selection with persistent point, tooltip, and lock icon, and a second click on the same point unlocks it.

## Step 1

Open {{portfolio_overview_url}} in a browser and wait for the Portfolio Overview workspace to finish loading with the Portfolio Performance card visible.

## Step 2

On the Portfolio Performance chart, hover a visible data point so its tooltip is available for selection.

## Step 3

Click the visible hovered chart point once and confirm the point stays visible, the tooltip stays visible, and a lock icon appears.

## Step 4

capture baseline: locked chart-point selection after the first click.

## Step 5

Click the same locked chart point a second time and confirm the lock icon disappears and the chart returns to an unlocked selection state.

## Step 6 — assert @verifies ac-24, ac-26, ac-27, ac-28, ac-29, ac-30

Confirm state-transition check: no locked chart-point selection (equals) — the stated promise: A second click on the locked chart point unlocks the selection.

> Prove pointer exit hides the tooltip after a hover interaction has displayed it.

## Step 2

On the Portfolio Overview page, store the current dashboard summary card values as baseline_summary_cards.

## Step 3

Hover a visible data point on the Portfolio Performance chart and confirm the custom tooltip is visible.

## Step 4

Store the visible hover tooltip state as baseline_visible_tooltip.

## Step 5

Move the pointer out of the chart plotting area.

## Step 6

Confirm the tooltip is no longer visible and the dashboard summary cards still match baseline_summary_cards.

## Step 7 — assert @verifies ac-14, ac-24, ac-39

Confirm 'tooltip after pointer leaves the chart' does NOT appear (forbidden-presence) — the stated promise: Pointer leaving the chart hides the tooltip.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Highest value because it covers the primary analytical action across all supported periods and verifies multiple core range-update promises.
[value_score] Very high value because custom tooltip content and summary-card stability are central to chart interpretation and likely to regress in interaction changes.
[value_score] High value because point lock/unlock is a custom interaction with multiple visible obligations that can break together.
[value_score] High value because stale locked state after a time-range change would mislead period-to-period analysis.
[value_score] Important first-load coverage for default state and required chart composition, but less interaction risk than the stateful paths.
[value_score] Important keyboard clearing path, but narrower in reach than click lock/unlock or range switching.
[value_score] Useful cleanup-path coverage for tooltip dismissal, but isolated to a single exit condition and lower impact than the main interaction paths.
[self_critique] The oracle proves the range-change promise by comparing stored pre-selection chart state to post-selection chart state, not merely by checking which chip is highlighted.

[self_critique] The hover test kept the technique aligned to interaction observables — tooltip presence, hover values, point styling, and stable summary cards — instead of over-broadly rechecking unrelated static chart structure.

[self_critique] A negative-case sweep found no source-backed invalid-input or error-handling behavior for time-range selection, so no extra negative scenario was minted beyond the forbidden default-tooltip and forbidden summary drift promises already covered.

[self_critique] The first-load test kept assertions narrow to defaults and required chart composition; lock clearing and pointer-exit behavior remained in their dedicated scenarios so a single broad test would not mask regressions.
